pr_title: Move unschedulable Pod to internal schedulingQ synchronously
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug
/sig scheduling

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

- use in-cache Pod instead of real-time Pod (by calling API server) to mark it as unschedulable
  in internal schedulingQ
- remove the backoff logic as now we don't call API server
- the whole logic is changed to a synchronous call

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #90616.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Fix a racing issue that scheduler may perform unnecessary scheduling attempt.
```

issue_context.title: Unnecessary scheduling attempt
issue_context.body:
When there is not any node fits for an incoming Pod, scheduler firstly tries to [put it to internal unschedulableQ or backoffQ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L504). And right after that, scheduler [updates the Pod's status as unschedulable](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L391-L396) via API server:

But unfortunately, the preceding step is running as a [goroutine](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L487), which in practice can happen after the latter step. Or even worse, the preceding step may occur after the PodUpdate event comes in. In this case, the logic that scheduler intentionally bypasses the updated Pod doesn't work (L439~L446 below won't be reached):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L436-L452

Then the Pod gets added to activeQ (L452 above) and will soon be retried - which in most cases is a waste as it was just tried earlier.

**Reproduce steps:**

See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/90616#issuecomment-621520874.

**Solutions:**

- Aggressive option. Change the [goroutine](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L487) to be synchronous call.
- Safe option.  Update `PriorityQueue#Update()` to guard the case: even if a Pod is not in unschedulingQ, it may also be unnecessary to be added into activeQ.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-longterm

We can use an integration test to reproduce this:

```diff
diff --git a/test/integration/scheduler/framework_test.go b/test/integration/scheduler/framework_test.go
index cf54a938e87..48798044520 100644
--- a/test/integration/scheduler/framework_test.go
+++ b/test/integration/scheduler/framework_test.go
@@ -1397,7 +1397,7 @@ func TestFilterPlugin(t *testing.T) {
 		scheduler.WithFrameworkOutOfTreeRegistry(registry))
 	defer testutils.CleanupTest(t, testCtx)
 
-	for _, fail := range []bool{false, true} {
+	for _, fail := range []bool{true} {
 		filterPlugin.failFilter = fail
 		// Create a best effort pod.
 		pod, err := createPausePod(testCtx.ClientSet,
@@ -1416,6 +1416,8 @@ func TestFilterPlugin(t *testing.T) {
 			}
 		}

 		if filterPlugin.numFilterCalled == 0 {
 			t.Errorf("Expected the filter plugin to be called.")
 		}
```

And then run the "TestFilterPlugin" test for 10 times, on my local dev machines, it shows like:

```script
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 2
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 4
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 4
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 2
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 2
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 2
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 4
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 2
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 2
    framework_test.go:1419: [DEBUG] filterPlugin.numFilterCalled = 2
```

The number shows Filter() function being called, as the test setups 2 node, so only 2 calls are expected, but you can see that 30% of the results shows 4 calls, and also there is error msa when adding the Pod to unschedubleQ:

```
E0429 16:14:44.771547   92995 factory.go:505] pod: filter-plugin929b921d-45bc-4472-810c-1622dfbe9331/test-pod is already present in the active queue
``` 

It also proves the racing symptom.

I think I prefer option 1.
It looks like the only reason why it's a goroutine instead of a synchronous call is the API request to get an updated pod.

But I think we shouldn't need it. If an update comes in while we were doing a scheduling cycle (with more changes than just status), the pod should go in the active queue, and then we don't need to add it to the unschedulable queue (and that shouldn't be an error). If otherwise we didn't get any updates, we just add the pod to the unschedulable queue.

This would save us not just the unnecessary scheduling attempt but an API call :)

> I think I prefer option 1.

I checked the asynchronous call's history, it was introduced 6 years ago... And the comment also assumed it was for temporary use. I think we should enough reasons to optimize it, just need to be cautious for regression. I will craft a PR.

> But I think we shouldn't need it.

I feel the same.

Aha, I found the trick here:

- `informerFactory` doesn't instantiate any informer when it's created (informers.NewSharedInformerFactory)
- `podInformer`, create by `informerFactory.Core().V1().Pods()` is nothing but a "hollow" interface - the concrete podInfomer and its indexer are not created yet
- when the real podInformer (and its indexer) is created? You're hearing right - by explicitly call `podInfomer.Informer()` or `podInfomer.Indexer()` - which will instantiate everything a podInformer needs. Otherwise, the podInformer will be only ready until call ErrFunc (by calling the informer's Lister() function), but by that time, informerFactory has already started for a while, so the informer doesn't really work.
- given the above fact, I really don't want the test to rely on such a tricky triggering point of podInformer.

> what if the pod gets updated while it was being processed?

This PR doesn't change how it's processed before, say:

- If the being processed Pod is schedulable, no matter the updated Pod is schedulable or not, the Pod finished its binding cycle and get its `nodeName` set.
- If the being processed Pod is unschedulable, putting it back to schedulingQ may conflict with the updated version, but it's fault tolerant. Next time when it's popped out, we have the latest copy.

> aren't we going to miss those updates since the pod is not in the queue at all?

This PR only put extra logic on delete case, so no changes on updated Pod.

> perhaps we can read the pod back from informer cache.

>If the being processed Pod is unschedulable, putting it back to schedulingQ may conflict with the updated version, but it's fault tolerant. Next time when it's popped out, we have the latest copy.

you may miss the update because the error function could have been called from the bind goroutine as I mentioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90660/files?file-filters%5B%5D=.go#r421165418, here is how this could happen in your original version:
1) pod is added to the queue
2) main thread pops the pod from the queue
3) update pod condition happens, but the event is missed because the pod is now not in the queue
